articles.title: Jeremiah Smith makes Heisman statement with latest outing in win over No. 14 Iowa: 'I'm the best player in the country'
articles.summary: Jeremiah Smith has racked up 423 receiving yards and six touchdowns in the past two weeks for the Buckeyes.
articles.body:
IOWA CITY, Iowa — Ryan Day knows he has a problem on his hands when it comes to Jeremiah Smith.

And after the star wide receiver put not only the rest of the Big Ten conference, but everyone else in the Heisman Trophy conversation, on notice Saturday, it's only going to get worse.

"Every coach in America is going to say, 'We've got to take this guy away,'" Day said.

Smith led No. 5 Ohio State to a dominant 31-14 win over No. 14 Iowa on Saturday afternoon, spoiling what was one of the biggest games at Kinnick Stadium in the past two decades. He had 206 yards and two touchdowns on 11 catches in the win, which marked his second consecutive 200-yard outing. Smith had a career-high 217 yards and four touchdowns in the Buckeyes' blowout win over Illinois last week.

Smith broke both the Ohio State receiving touchdowns record and the school's receptions record in the process. He already held the yardage record, so Smith holds all three major categories for a wide receiver in Columbus.

The last two outings are the only times that Smith has surpassed 200 receiving yards in a single game in his career. He also entered Saturday as the nation's leader in receiving yards, and tied for the most in receiving touchdowns.

"I just want more, really," Smith said. "I'm never satisfied."

It's not just the numbers that Smith is putting up that is turning heads. It's how he's doing it.

There was one play on Saturday in which Ohio State quarterback Julian Sayin threw into triple coverage, and the ball somehow made it through to Smith. He turned it into a 54-yard gain. Fittingly, that was the 200th catch of his career.

Smith, Day and Sayin all laughed about that after the game, and admitted that the ball should not have been thrown. They got lucky.

"That throw, I didn't expect Julian to throw that one. I was surprised he threw it," Smith said. "But it just shows we have trust in each other, and he expects me to make that play. That's exactly what I'm going to do."

He did it again later, too, making a grab with two defenders — one of them was called for a holding penalty — all over him.

The final touchdown of the day, though, he was wide open.

And once he reached the back of the end zone, Smith hit the Heisman celebration.

"There's times where he's covered, and we still make the throw and catch," Day said. "It just speaks to his ability, and Julian's trust with him. But then there's other plays where he was open … The only way that that works is if he practices the way he does to work through all the issues and timing that comes with it and all the basics. I can't say enough about who he is as a person."

Iowa coach Kirk Ferentz quickly compared him to Philadelphia Eagles star and former Penn State standout Saquon Barkley in terms of how dominant he is as a player.

"We gave him everything we had, and he's still pretty effective. … All you can do is do your best and try to be as smart as you can playing him," Ferentz said. "He's a great player.

"With a little bit of luck, we won't see him again in my career."

Ohio State now sits at 4-1 after Saturday's win. The Buckeyes will take on Maryland at home next weekend before a tough three-game stretch that includes road games at No. 6 Indiana and No. 18 USC, and a home battle with No. 15 Oregon.

All three of those opponents are sure to try and find different ways to at least slow Smith down, something that's been just about impossible so far this fall. The only game in which he's been held below 150 receiving yards this season was their blowout 59-3 win over Kent State.

Though the team's conference title and postseason aspirations are very real, Smith has something else on his mind, too. And after Saturday, he's now likely out in front in that race.

"I just gotta keep the Heisman voters, or whoever it is, [aware] that I'm the best player in the country," he said plainly.

articles.title: Rhode Island football wins Governor's Cup in nail-biter against Brown
articles.summary: Brown had all the momentum, until Ty Groff's 43-yard field goal with 11 seconds sealed the win for URI at Centreville Bank Stadium on Oct. 3, 2026.
articles.body:
PAWTUCKET – Ty Groff had a feeling he might get one last chance, and the University of Rhode Island kicker made the most of it.

His second 43-yard field goal on this Saturday afternoon came with 11 seconds to play, and it returned the Governor's Cup to the Rams after a year-long absence.

Brown missed out on a golden opportunity to win consecutive games in this rivalry for the first time in a decade. It was URI celebrating under the sunshine at Centreville Bank Stadium thanks to this 13-10 squirmer.

The Rams punted with 1:19 left to pin the Bears inside their own 20 and used their defense to record a quick three-and-out. URI started in prime field position at the Brown 46 with 32 seconds left and benefited from a personal foul that brought the ball within Groff's range. His line-drive kick sailed through the uprights, and the Rams hoisted the silver trophy at midfield, courtesy of Gov. Dan McKee.

"I would say it's just trusting myself," Groff said. "I've had a lot of ups and downs in my life, whether it was high school or college. It's all about belief."

URI had possession in a 10-10 game earlier in the fourth quarter and moved the ball across midfield before facing a second fourth down on the drive. The Rams elected to kick it away, and Randy Leavitt dropped one softly to the Bears 12. Brown gained two yards on a Matt Childs rush and threw a pair of incomplete passes – Andre DePina-Gray deflected the second one in the backfield to force a Bears punt.

"I just couldn't be more proud of everybody," URI coach Jim Fleming said. "That's what every coach says, but our kids had a resolve today. They were not going to be denied."

Brown posted a 28-21 victory here last season to snap a six-game losing streak in the series and looked poised to do it again in front of 5,368 fans. The Bears generated three turnovers and used a 1-yard Qwentin Brown touchdown run with 13:29 left to take a 10-3 lead. Brown couldn't find a finishing touch down the stretch and followed a 14-10 defeat against Harvard here with another.

"It's a challenge, because you lose two close games in a row," Brown coach James Perry said. "They're mature kids. We'll be ready to go next week."

The Bears seemed to have all the momentum after Tommy Dunn's power rush off the defense's left edge forced URI quarterback Tyler Budge's second fumble of the afternoon. Dunn recovered himself at the Rams 13 and Childs picked up a fourth down before Brown slammed into the end zone. The Rams stopped their quarterback rotation at that point and went exclusively to former Barrington standout Alex McClelland, who authored each of the last two scoring drives.

"I told the guys pregame both my parents went to Brown, and it just kind of rubbed me the wrong way that they didn't want me," McClelland said. "More than happy to be with these guys right here and this coach."

URI's second play on the ensuing series saw McClelland look for a fellow All-State pick from seasons past. He found Marquis Buchanan running free down the middle, and the Classical alum – who came in nursing a right knee injury and left briefly in the first quarter – sped 68 yards to the Bears 12. McClelland took it himself the rest of the way at the game was knotted again with 12:05 left.

"[Buchanan is] so tough," Fleming said. "People don't know that. He's one of those pretty guys who catches a lot of touchdowns – no. That's a tough dude."

Brown had a chance to reclaim the lead on the ensuing drive. The Bears rattled off nine plays before facing a fourth and five at the Rams 23 and declined to give Drew Crabtree a chance at a 40-yard field goal. James Murphy rolled right and found Levi Linowes for nine yards, but two penalties on the play – the second for a chop block in the backfield – pushed Brown out of range and forced a punt.

"All those decisions are very tight," Perry said. "We have a very good kicker – that's a long one. At this level, anything over 40 is long."

Groff's first make with 18 seconds left in the first half gave URI (3-3) a 3-0 lead into halftime. The Rams staggered on offense with Buchanan, Terrence Campbell (right ankle) and Aboraa Kwarteng (left leg) all on the sidelines but leaned on their defense to remain in contact. The Bears finished the day with just 35 rushing yards on 26 carries and threw an interception to Ethan McCann-Carter in the third quarter.

"We've had this one circled for a long time," URI defensive lineman Case Mankins said. "We had to go get it for coach."

Brown (1-2) used a big hit on the perimeter from Brock Owen to force Budge's first fumble inside its own 10, and the Bears followed with their best drive to that point. EJ Perez's recovery set up a Murphy scramble out of jail for 13 yards and a pass down the middle to Childs for 27 yards. Crabtree's 33-yard field goal with 3:11 left in the third made it a 3-3 game, and Brown seemed a couple of possessions away from shaking a URI team looking to avoid three straight defeats for the first time since 2021.

"We played a very tight football game with a quality opponent, a rival, and found a way to beat them," Fleming said. "We've got the cup sitting in Kingston where it will stay."

RI – Alex McClelland 12 run (Groff kick)

Passing: B, 21-37-1 271 (James Murphy 21-37-1 271); RI, 16-26-1 157 (Alex McClelland 6-11-0 83, Tyler Budge 10-15-1 74).

Rushing: B, 26-35 (Matt Childs 13-37, Qwentin Brown 3-3); RI, 50-217 (Gabe Winowich 23-85, BJ Barrow 8-42).

Receiving: B, 21-271 (Childs 6-64, Pearson Hill 4-33, Jadon Garza-Pender 3-66); RI, 16-157 (Marquis Buchanan 5-90, Kevin Green Jr. 3-20, Sean Byrd 2-36).

articles.title: Jeremiah Smith Drops Confident Quote Amid Heisman Hype After Making History in OSU's Win vs. Iowa
articles.summary: Ohio State wide receiver Jeremiah Smith sent a message to Heisman Trophy voters after his impressive performance during the No. 5 Buckeyes' 31-14 victory over No. 14 Iowa on Saturday.
articles.body:
Ohio State wide receiver Jeremiah Smith sent a message to Heisman Trophy voters after his impressive performance during the No. 5 Buckeyes' 31-14 victory over No. 14 Iowa on Saturday.

"Just gotta keep the Heisman voters or whoever it is know that I'm the best player in the country, so I gotta be there," Smith told reporters after the game (0:08 mark).

The 20-year-old caught 11 passes for 206 yards and two touchdowns against the Hawkeyes.

Smith set Ohio State's all-time receiving touchdowns record as well as the school's all-time receptions record in the third quarter of the contest. He already holds the Buckeyes' all-time receiving yards record.

He hit a Heisman Trophy pose after his record-breaking score.

Ohio State head coach Ryan Day praised Smith after the victory.

"As you can imagine, drawing plays up for him is a lot of fun," Day told CBS Sports' Jenny Dell. "But the most amazing thing about Jeremiah Smith is his work ethic every day. How much he loves to win, how competitive he is, the way he works every day, the example he sets. Not only is he a great player, he's become a great leader. I've challenged him before, like it isn't just about you, it's about the team and he's been brought up that way his whole life. That's just his mindset."

Smith was already in the Heisman conversation heading into Saturday's action, as he racked up 617 receiving yards and seven touchdown catches while averaging 18.7 yards per reception across his first four games of the year.

He's attempting become the first Ohio State player to capture the Heisman Trophy since Troy Smith in 2006.

articles.title: 'El juego por dentro': Rafa Guerrero, psicólogo, y la salud mental de nuestros deportistas
articles.standfirst: Escúchalo gratis en Spotify, Ivoox, Apple Podcast, Omny, MARCA.com y Radio MARCA
articles.summary: Escúchalo gratis en Spotify, Ivoox, Apple Podcast, Omny, MARCA.com y Radio MARCA
articles.body: MARCA estrena el segundo episodio de la nueva temporada de 'El Juego por Dentro' con Rafa Guerrero, psicólogo, psicoterapeuta, divulgador y autor de 23 libros, el último de ellos 'Adictos a las pantallas'. Guerrero, especialista en vínculos, apego, trauma y autoestima, repasa en el podcast cómo se gestiona la presión en el deporte, desde la base hasta la élite. Preguntado directamente por el estado de la salud mental de los deportistas profesionales, Guerrero no se anda con rodeos: "¿Cómo está la salud mental de nuestros deportistas de élite? Mal, francamente mal". Según explica, los niveles de ansiedad y depresión están disparados en la población general, en una tendencia que atribuye en parte a la pandemia, aunque advierte de que el problema es anterior. Los deportistas de élite, señala, forman parte de esta realidad, pero afrontan además las particularidades y presiones propias del deporte profesional. El psicólogo pone el foco también en los adultos que rodean a los niños y adolescentes que empiezan en el deporte. "Somos los adultos, los que metemos toda esa presión y toda esa expectativa", señala, y apunta directamente a un patrón que ve con frecuencia en consulta: padres que proyectan en sus hijos ambiciones propias no cumplidas. Guerrero cita el caso de Andrés Iniesta, que reconoció haber sufrido depresión en la cima de su carrera, para ilustrar que el éxito deportivo no protege de estos problemas. La conversación también aborda la identidad del deportista más allá de la competición, con el caso de Michael Phelps como referencia, y el fenómeno de las adicciones sin sustancia —redes sociales, trabajo, pantallas— que Guerrero desarrolla en su último libro. "La adicción no es el problema, la adicción es la solución que esta persona con adicción tiene", explica, defendiendo una mirada sin juicio hacia quienes las padecen. El Juego por Dentro, el videopodcast de bienestar mental y emocional en el deporte, está disponible en las principales plataformas de podcast (Spotify, Ivoox, Apple Podcast, Omny…) y también en MARCA.com y Radio MARCA. Suscríbete gratis en tu plataforma habitual para no perderte ningún episodio. Mantiene una periodicidad quincenal, con nuevos episodios cada dos semanas en los que deportistas, exdeportistas, psicólogos y expertos en rendimiento comparten su experiencia sobre mentalidad, gestión emocional, presión, liderazgo y crecimiento personal. Una propuesta interesante para profundizar en cómo funciona la mente del deportista y qué hay realmente detrás del rendimiento.

articles.title: Colorado State parts ways with defensive coordinator Tyson Summers during 56-26 loss to Oregon State
articles.summary: Summers was replaced as the team's defensive play caller in the first half.
articles.body:
Colorado State made an abrupt change at defensive coordinator on Saturday night.

After the Rams lost 56-26 at home to Oregon State, Colorado State coach Jim Mora Jr. told reporters that the team had parted ways with defensive coordinator Tyson Summers.

However, that parting appeared to happen during the game and not after it.

Mora said that Summers was replaced as the team's defensive play caller during the first half of the blowout loss and multiple reporters noted that he did not return to the sideline.

"Tyson was relieved of his play-calling duties. He left the field and he is no longer with this football program," Mora said in his postgame media session, before following up with "that is a permanent."

Summers was replaced by assistant coach Kenny McClendon as the team's play caller. Per CBS Sports, McClendon will be the team's new defensive coordinator.

The loss dropped Colorado State to 2-3 and also further solidified the Rams' status as one of the worst defenses in the country. Entering Week 5, Colorado State ranked 129th out of 138 in scoring defense, allowing 34.2 points per game. And, somehow, the defense was letting up 7.4 yards a play.

Oregon State had 727 yards of total offense on 71 plays Saturday. QB Braden Atkinson was 30-of-34 passing for 413 yards and five TDs, while the Beavers rushed 36 times for 291 yards as a team.

Summers and Mora were in their first year together after Mora was hired as Colorado State's coach at the end of the 2025 season. Summers was Colorado State's defensive coordinator in 2025 under Jay Norvell and was the team's interim coach after Norvell was fired midway through the season. He came to CSU after numerous stops as a defensive assistant following a two-year tenure in charge of Georgia Southern in 2016 and 2017.

articles.title: Colorado State Fires DC Tyson Summers After Mid-Game Replacement in Loss vs. Oregon State
articles.summary: Colorado State head coach Jim Mora announced Saturday that defensive coordinator Tyson Summers was fired following the team's 56-26 loss against Oregon State.
articles.body:
Colorado State head coach Jim Mora announced Saturday that defensive coordinator Tyson Summers was fired following the team's 56-26 loss against Oregon State.

Kenny McClendon took over the defensive play-calling during that contest and Mora said that Summers "left the field" after the demotion.

After starting 2-0, the Rams have lost three straight, giving up an average of 52 points per game in defeats against BYU, UTSA and Oregon State.

Beavers' quarterback Braden Atkinson shredded the Colorado State defense on Saturday to the tune of 413 yards and five touchdowns through the air, completing 30 of 34 passes. That came one week after UTSA put up 542 yards of total offense and 59 points on the Rams' defense, and two weeks after BYU rushed for a staggering 332 yards against them.

Summers, 46, was in his second stint as the school's defensive coordinator, a role he first held for a season in 2015 before becoming the head coach at Georgia Southern. He returned to Fort Collins in 2025 as the defensive coordinator and also operated as the interim head coach for five games after Jay Norvell was fired.

Mora was then hired and kept Summers aboard to lead the defense. It was a short relationship, however, and there was plenty of foreshadowing that a divorce was inevitable—leading into this week's matchup against Oregon State, Mora made it abundantly clear that he was expecting Summers to simplify his defensive scheme.

"Players at any level, regardless of intelligence, can only comprehend so much in a football game. It's chaos," he told reporters . "When you get in situations where your players aren't playing fast because they're not certain, it's critically important that you shrink the package."

"That's why I say we have to do a better job. We can't wait to change things. It's too late and that's not fair to our players," he added. "You have to be ultra-demanding of your players but you have to be specific about what you're demanding of them. It's not easy. It's complicated, but we have to un-complicate it."

That apparently didn't happen to Mora's liking, to the point that Summers is no longer with the program.

articles.title: Deion Sanders, Colorado vs. Texas Tech Final Box Score, Top Player Stats and Highlights
articles.summary: Make it three losses in a row for Deion Sanders and his Colorado Buffaloes.
articles.body:
Make it three losses in a row for Deion Sanders and his Colorado Buffaloes.

Texas Tech went into Boulder and walked away with a 29-7 win, completely shutting down the Buffs' offense after allowing a touchdown on the game's opening drive.

It was a rough starting debut for Isaac Wilson, who took over at quarterback this week after Julian Lewis struggled. Colorado put a heavy workload on him, as he rushed the ball 17 times and threw it 44 times, though his three interceptions (and one pick-six) didn't make the strongest case for keeping the starting gig going forward.

Colorado finished with four turnovers overall and missed two field goals. It was, in a word, brutal.

On the other side of the ball, Texas Tech didn't exactly impress either, finishing with less overall yards than the Buffs (375-315) while finishing just 3-of-12 on third down. But Texas Tech was able to control the game on the ground (181 rushing yards), didn't turn the ball over once and actually converted their field-goal attempts.

Sometimes games are won and sometimes they are lost. Texas Tech did what was needed to win this one, but Colorado did more than enough to lose several times over.

The Red Raiders (5-0) now get a bye week before hosting Arizona State on Oct. 17. Colorado (2-3) will try to end their losing streak in two weeks when they host No. 13 Utah.

No. 11 LSU put together a dominant performance during a lopsided 63-14 win over McNeese State on Saturday night.

Head coach Lane Kiffin's squad secured a blowout victory after entering the game as 54.5-point favorites, according to FanDuel Sportsbook .

The Tigers set the tone early on Saturday, as an interception by safety Tamarcus Cooley turned into a 48-yard touchdown drive that gave LSU a 7-0 lead to start the first quarter.

Kiffin's team didn't show any signs of slowing down afterwards, jumping out to a 35-0 advantage at halftime.

The Tigers led by 49 points in the second half before McNeese State was able to get on the board, eventually cruising to the win.

LSU was efficient offensively throughout the contest, scoring at least 14 points in each quarter of the game. The Tigers picked up 367 rush yards as a team, averaging 6.9 yards per carry.

While LSU's defense only forced one turnover, it consistently prevented McNeese State from moving the chains. The Cowboys finished the game with a mere six first downs, converting just one of 12 opportunities on third down.

After the Tigers suffered a tough loss to Ole Miss on Sept. 19, they've won two consecutive games while outscoring their opponents 98-20.

With Saturday's victory, LSU improved to 4-1.

articles.title: Wales v Denmark: Craig Bellamy's side aim to thrive in Nations League A
articles.summary: Captain Ben Davies says Wales will be driven by determination to prove they can live with challenges of Nations League A when they face Denmark in Cardiff.
articles.body:
Captain Ben Davies says Wales will be driven by a determination to prove they can thrive in Nations League A when they face Denmark in Cardiff on Sunday.

Wales go into the game in buoyant mood after ending a six-game winless sequence by taking the scalp of Norway on Thursday.

But having registered Wales' first ever victory in the Nations League's top tier, Craig Bellamy's players are hungry for more.

"We don't want to be in a situation where you feel like you're not competing against bigger teams," said defender Davies.

"But I thought we laid a good marker down the other night [against Norway] to show that we do belong playing against these teams - it was a much better all-round performance.

"I think we really got back to what's got us to success and got us into the Nations League A in the first place. Hopefully we can replicate that [against Denmark]."

Live on BBC iPlayer, BBC Two Wales, BBC Sounds, BBC Radio Wales, Radio Cymru and 5 Live, BBC Sport website and app, plus live text commentary.

Wales came from behind against Norway to secure a 2-1 success which eased the pressure built during their run without a win, which stretched back to the thrashing of North Macedonia last November.

Defeat against Bosnia-Herzegovina in the World Cup play-off semi-final came next, before friendly draws against Northern Ireland and Ghana were followed by successive defeats to Romania, Portugal and the Danes.

That left Bellamy and his players in need of a result as they met Norway, and they responded by delivering a rousing display.

Wales' cause was helped by Norway defender Torbjorn Heggem's red card early in the second half, but they had troubled the World Cup quarter-finalists even before the sending off.

"The teams at this level are all strong," added 103-cap Tottenham defender Davies.

"All the games are going to be tough but we're here to compete and here to try to give the best account of us that we can.

"I thought we did that the other night and it was really pleasing to get the three points. It gives us, as a group, a lot of confidence going into the games coming up."

Group has 'exploded' after Wales win - Bellamy

Why beating Denmark matters to Wales' Euro 2028 hopes

Wales will again be without the likes of Karl Darlow, Joe Rodon, Dylan Lawlor, David Brooks and Harry Wilson because of injury as they look to maintain the momentum gained thanks to the Norway triumph.

Bellamy says he has no choice but to make changes to the side which began on Thursday as Wales seek to make amends for last Sunday's defeat in Denmark.

Having emerged with some credit despite losing their Nations League opener against Portugal 10 days ago, Wales were well beaten on a demoralising evening in Copenhagen.

Davies hopes the Cardiff City Stadium factor will be key as Wales chase victory against a Danish side who, in 21st, are 17 places above them in the Fifa rankings.

"It does make a big difference going away. We didn't get a grip on the game [in Denmark] whereas when we played Norway in Cardiff, it's our home, our fans, our atmosphere," he said.

"It felt like a different game and we had much more control… you just know you have to try to make your home advantage count."

articles.title: El Camp Nou reactiva el carrusel de Clásicos
articles.standfirst: Barcelona y Real Madrid se enfrentan este domingo por primera vez sin Alexia Putellas, máxima goleadora; ni Misa Rodríguez, única en jugarlos todos
articles.summary: Barcelona y Real Madrid se enfrentan este domingo por primera vez sin Alexia Putellas, máxima goleadora; ni Misa Rodríguez, única en jugarlos todos
articles.body: Barcelona y Real Madrid se enfrentan este domingo (finalmente a las 19:00 horas por las condiciones meteorológicas) en el Camp Nou en partido correspondiente a la sexta jornada de la Liga F, competición que dominan las azulgrana aventajando en dos puntos a las blancas. Un Clásico, el primero del curso, que es el número 26 en el carrusel de enfrentamientos entre ambos conjuntos y que viene marcado por diferentes nombres propios. Dos de ellos, Alexia Putellas y Misa Rodríguez, serán protagonistas en la distancia. La que fuera capitana azulgrana es la máxima goleadora en la historia de los Clásicos con 15 goles. La dos veces Balón de Oro anotó seis goles en Liga, uno en la Copa de la Reina, tres en la Supercopa de España y cinco en Champions League, dos de ellos en el Camp Nou. La de Mollet del Vallès verá el duelo como espectadora una vez que el verano pasado fichara por el London City Lionesses. "Intento ver los partidos como aficionada, pero no puedo. Son mix excompañeras, tengo muchas amigas allí a las que quiero muchísimo y a la vez es el Barça", aseguró recientemente en una entrevista en RadioMARCA. La que fuera capitana blanca, actualmente en el Arsenal, es la única futbolista que hasta la fecha ha disputado todos los Clásicos celebrados hasta la fecha. Misa participó en los 25 duelos ante el Barcelona, en los que encajó un total de 92 goles (3.68 de media), dando la cara muchas veces tras las derrotas de su equipo. "Nos duele y nos avergüenza no haber estado a la altura", aseguró tras el último envite. Alexia, Misa, Jenni, Weir, Mapi, Ivana, Salma, Olga... todas ellos son historia, pero pasado de los Clásicos. La nueva temporada trae consigo nuevos nombres en los que poner el foco. "Es un gran partido para todos los culés, especial para nosotras, es un Clásico y lo afrontamos con muchas ganas", admitió la azulgrana Clara Serrajordi. Los dos equipos llegan invictos al duelo, el Barcelona sumando siete victorias en siete partidos y el Real Madrid con un bagaje de seis triunfos y tres empates. "Ya hemos vivido varios Clásicos, unos más ajustados que otros. El Madrid se va reforzando año tras año y va creciendo al igual que nosotras. Creo que será un partido entre los dos mejores equipo de la Liga. Todo el mundo que lo vea disfrutará del fútbol", afirmó Claudia Pina. Será un encuentro marcado por los numerosos duelos individuales que puede dar de sí. Caroline Graham y Linda Caicedo parten a priori como jugadoras a llevar el timón de sus equipos. La noruega firma 14 participaciones de gol en siete partidos (seis goles y ocho asistencias) y llega con la flechita hacia arriba, mientras que la colombiana, con tres dianas, es de las que se crece en partidos grandes. "Siempre queremos ganar al Madrid. Es un Clásico. Lo afrontamos con las máximas ganas y ellas seguramente también", dijo Caro. "Jugar contra el Madrid te da esa motivación extra porque es divertido. El fútbol femenino necesita esta rivalidad", añadió. "Estoy en un buen momento, disfrutando, pero siempre se puede mejorar", subrayó. Kerolin Nicoli y Felicia Schröder son los fichajes millonarios acometidos por Barcelona y Real Madrid este verano. A la brasileña le está costando encontrar su sitio en el once azulgrana -a priori, Romeu cuenta con ella en el extremo zurdo- si bien ya se ha estrenado con un gol en Europa (ante el Paris FC); la sueca, por su parte, ha caído de pie y lleva ocho dianas, siendo la máxima goleadora del conjunto blanco, habiendo marcado en todos los encuentros que ha jugado a excepción del duelo ante el City del jueves. En la portería estará el foco en Cata Coll y Merle Frohms. "El Real Madrid está jugando bien, con confianza, pero nosotras también. Venimos de menos a más y de hacer un gran partido en Roma. Creo que será un duelo disputado y bonito de ver para los aficionados", aseveró la guardameta azulgrana, que elogió el paso adelante dado por el eterno rival. "Se han reforzado bien, con grandes fichajes, han apostado por hacer un buen equipo y creo que están en la línea correcta", subrayó. Será el reencuentro de las campeonas del mundo Sub'20. Aïcha Camara, Carla Julià, Noe Jiménez y Rosalía Domínguez por parte azulgrana, siendo la primera la única con experiencias en Clásicos; y Laia López, Silvia Cristóbal, Noe Bejarano, Pau Comendador e Irune Dorado por el bando blanco, siendo las dos últimas las únicas que han participado en duelos ante el primer equipo del Barcelona. Otro nombre propio al que apuntarán los focos será el de María Planes. La colegiada murciana, de 29 años, ha sido designada por el CTA para el partido entre Barcelona y Real Madrid del Camp Nou, siendo el primer Clásico que dirige en su carrera. Hasta la fecha, Planes ha pitado en ocho ocasiones al Barcelona con un bagaje de siete victorias y un empate; y en 13 ocasiones al Real Madrid, saldándose siempre los encuentros con victoria blanca. Será la primera vez que el Camp Nou abra sus puertas para un Clásico liguero y la tercera vez que ambos equipos se vean las caras en el coliseo azulgrana, que anteriormente fue escenario de dos compromisos de Champions League. La vuelta de los cuartos de final de 2022, con triunfo azulgrana (5-2) y récord mundial de aforo (91.553 espectadores) -que se batiría (91.648) en semifinales ante el Wolfsburgo-; y la misma ronda de la edición de 2025, con triunfo azulgrana (6-0). "Fueron días muy especiales que nunca olvidaremos", confiesa Patri Guijarro, capitana azulgrana. "Sabemos que hay muchas entradas vendidas y eso es buena noticia para nosotras", subraya. Aunque no se espera que el registro de aforo se acerque a estas cifras, sí que se espera que haya una gran entrada para este primer Barcelona-Real Madrid del curso.

articles.title: Quique sitúa al Alavés en otra dimensión
articles.standfirst: El técnico madrileño ha dado un cambio radical al conjunto vitoriano esta temporada
articles.summary: El técnico madrileño ha dado un cambio radical al conjunto vitoriano esta temporada
articles.body: El primer proyecto de Quique Sánchez Flores en Vitoria progresa adecuadamente. La mejoría del Alavés con respecto a la pasada temporada es una realidad y la mano del técnico madrileño se nota en un equipo que logró 10 puntos en las primeras cuatro jornadas para firmar el mejor estreno de su historia en Primera. Las dos derrotas consecutivas ante Racing y Valencia le devolvieron a la tierra, pero el empate obtenido en el derbi de San Mamés le ha permitido irse al parón con un buen sabor de boca... y en puestos europeos. El salto de calidad del Alavés está en el apartado defensivo. Los babazorros son el equipo menos goleado de la categoría, junto con Athletic y Celta, y han dejado su puerta a cero en tres de las siete jornadas. Nada que ver con los 20 partidos que encadenó el año pasado recibiendo algún tanto. Quique ha moldeado la mentalidad defensiva de un equipo que se siente más cómodo con el 5-3-2 y que ha fortalecido su mandíbula para soportar los golpes del rival. En clave ofensiva, el Alavés continúa siendo un equipo que produce muchas situaciones de gol y que tiene facilidad para generar peligro a través del centro lateral. Boyé y Toni Martínez continúan siendo dos piezas claves en el engranaje ofensivo de Quique, que ha recuperado para la causa a un renacido Mariano Díaz. La figura de Pablo Ibáñez, Ángel Pérez o Antonio Blanco es clave para que toda la maquinaria funcione, sin olvidar a Tenaglia, el corazón del vestuario. Es su estadio el principal elemento que le ha elevado a un lugar privilegiado en este inicio de curso. Todas sus victorias han llegado en Vitoria, donde ha hecho 9 goles en 4 partidos. Getafe, Villarreal y Osasuna se marcharon de vacío de su visita a Mendizorroza, que vuelve a tener un ambiente espectacular que supone una motivación extra para un equipo que juega de memoria cada vez que pisa su campo. La temporada no ha hecho más que empezar y conviene mantener la cautela, pero es evidente que el Alavés sueña con huir de la parte baja y reducir el estrés en el tramo final de curso. De momento, va por buen camino. La solidez defensiva de un equipo que ha recuperado el orden y el rigor táctico para conceder menos situaciones de peligro al rival y aumentar su capacidad para dejar la puerta a cero. La asignatura pendiente del Alavés vuelve a estar a domicilio. Los de Quique completaron dos buenos partidos como visitantes tanto en Butarque como en San Mamés, pero no les dio para ganar. Hasta ahora, sus victorias han sido en Mendizorroza. El Alavés ha llegado al parón de septiembre en sexta posición. Una posición privilegiada que sitúa al equipo en puesto europeos. La nota es un notable alto. Mariano era un caso perdido y estaba más fuera que dentro del Alavés al término del pasado curso, pero no ha tirado la toalla y ha sabido encontrar su momento. Ha marcado 3 goles en este arranque liguero y su papel está siendo determinante. Las lesiones han amargado la buena trayectoria del 'Glorioso' en este inicio. Quique perdió a Mikel Rodríguez y Garcés en el mismo entrenamiento después de que ambos sufrieran una rotura de ligamento cruzado anterior. Dos bajas sensibles que obligarán a Sergio Fernández a intervenir en el próximo mercado de invierno.

articles.title: Racing: Necesita tiempo para acoplarse
articles.standfirst: El técnico del conjunto cántabro pide paciencia
articles.summary: El técnico del conjunto cántabro pide paciencia
articles.body: El Racing de José Alberto ha sido fiel en este inicio de campaña al estilo que le hizo ascender a Primera división. Juego combinativo, con mucha presencia en campo rival y descuidando en muchas ocasiones las tareas defensivas. Este estilo ofensivo al Racing le está saliendo bien como local, pero mal como visitante. En El Sardinero suma 7 puntos dejando una buena imagen, mientras fuera de casa cuenta sus 4 partidos por derrotas, además con dos goleadas de escándalo en sus choque ante el Barcelona y Celta. José Alberto ha dejado claro que la mayoría de los fichajes han llegado en los últimos días antes del cierre del mercado por lo que pide 'paciencia' para que la plantilla coja los automatismos necesarios para competir en la máxima categoría. De los fichajes llegados este verano destaca por encima de todos Zabiri. el delantero marroquí que ya ha debutado con su selección, ha anotado 6 goles y está dejando muy buenas sensaciones. El resto de incorporaciones están adaptándose, aunque Pablo García ya marcó frente al Rayo Vallecano y ha dejado detalles de su calidad. En el lado negativo está André Almeida que fue expulsado en su debut ante el Alavés y dejó malas sensaciones frente al Celta al ser responsable de dos de los tantos vigueses por pérdidas en salida de balón. Sergio Canales ha entrado con buen pie en este nuevo Racing. El futbolista cántabro está llamado a ser el líder de este tipo jugando en el doble pivote o en la media punta por delante de los centrocampistas. Canales ya marcó de libre directo ante el Rayo Vallecano demostrando el guante que tiene en su pierna izquierda. Otro de los aspectos que va a tener el Racing a favor esta campaña es el apoyo incondicional de la afición. El Sardinero ha presentado entradas rozando el lleno y la afición cántabra ha viajado en masa en las salidas del equipo. Esta comunión de plantilla y afición puede ser positiva en los momentos claves de esta temporada. El Racing como local, no ha perdido y ha sumado 7/9 puntos ganando a Elche y Alavés y empatando con el Villarreal. El Racing como visitante, 4 partidos 4 derrotas. Además con las dos dolorosas goleadas ante Barcelona y Celta. La nota es un 6. A pesar de la decepción de las últimas jornadas, el Racing es un recién ascendido y no está en puestos de descenso. Zabiri, buena irrupción con 6 goles hasta la fecha. Íñigo Vicente también ha comenzado bien, pero solo en El Sardinero. Hasta la fecha Andre Almeida. En el debut fue expulsado por una entrada dura a un rival y cuando fue titular ante el Celta perdió los dos balones que costaron los primeros goles del club gallego.

articles.title: CR7 no es un cínico
articles.standfirst: El borde del área, por José Luis Hurtado
articles.summary: El borde del área, por José Luis Hurtado
articles.body: Aver. El periodismo, un oficio en el que se ven tipos que pavonean como Walter Matthau cuando simula ser el logo de la cabecera del Chicago Examiner en Primera Plana, no es la mejor parcela para solicitar humildad. Una estrella como la de Cristiano Ronaldo no se esculpe con modestia. Los tiempos modernos recetan dosis de soberbia, altivez y frases para TikTok. El CR7 podría ser un automóvil, un cohete de la NASA, el nombre clave de un espía, un ron, pero es una multinacional con botas de fútbol al que Jorge Jesus, el seleccionador portugués, con el aspecto de cantante en piscinas, ha relegado al banquillo. En su ruta mental, CR7 cree que todavía merece el Balón de Oro. Verse en el banquillo le supone una humillación. Para su marca es peor esa imagen que perder una final. Hay momentos que valen por una biopsia. En una secuencia de la película Ronaldo, un documento aberrante e imprescindible, el futbolista lleva a su hijo al garaje de casa para que elija el coche que van a utilizar. En ese establecimiento, más grande que alguna aldea, se amontonaban los coches de lujo. A alguien le pareció una idea formidable no cortar esa escena en el montaje final. Desde hace años se sabía que habría salseo cuando un entrenador bajara a CR7 a la Tierra. El máximo goleador de la historia del Real Madrid contraprogramó la conquista de una Champions sobre el mismo césped al anunciar su adiós del club. En esos regímenes de impunidad, sólo aptos para divos, Michael Jordan insultaba desde el fondo del autobús al mánager general de los Chicago Bulls, Jerry Krause, al que tachaba de gordo, pero es que era Jordan. Alí, uno de los monumentos deportivos y sociales de la historia, utilizaba la lengua como una guillotina. Se creía “el más grande”, una etiqueta que era un adhesivo a su personalidad, pero es que era Alí. CR7 tiene que jugar porque es CR7. Insaciable, voraz e histriónico, sólo a él, un maniaco de la competitividad, se le podía ocurrir desafiar durante una década a Messi. Otros se habrían rendido, él comprendió que eso era una puerta para la celebridad. Ahora, lo último que necesitaba alguien como CR7 era una cifra tóxica en los flecos del horizonte. Los mil goles se han convertido en una razón para respirar. En tiempos de cinismo atómico, CR7 es transparente, se exhibe tal y como es. Tal vez sea complicado ser humilde con 679 millones de seguidores en Instagram.

articles.summary: Early season upstarts Florida and Mississippi State have been two of the biggest stories in college football, but both teams were humbled in lopsided losses to Missouri and Alabama.
articles.body:
Early season upstarts Florida and Mississippi State have been two of the biggest stories in college football, but both teams were humbled in lopsided losses to Missouri and Alabama.

In the weekend's other matchup of ranked opponents, Ohio State's offense was too much for Iowa's defense, giving the Buckeyes another strong counterpoint to their Texas loss.

All of that led to plenty of shuffling in our weekly rankings, and ahead is an updated look at how the college football experts here at B/R line up the nation's top 25 teams following Week 5 action.

25. Boise State (4-1, Previous Rank: 25)

Week 5 Result: WIN vs. Utah State (37-18) Next Week: at Fresno State

The Broncos jumped out to a 21-0 lead with touchdowns on each of their first three drives, and that proved to be an insurmountable lead in a 37-18 victory. Maddux Madsen (17/21, 244 yards, 2 TD, 0 INT) and Dylan Riley (18 carries, 93 yards, 2 TD) both had strong games offensively, while the defense tallied nine tackles for loss, six sacks, one takeaway and a pick six. They are looking more and more like a team capable of running the table the rest of the way following their Week 1 loss to Oregon.

The Ducks pulled out a win over USC, but saw starting quarterback Dante Moore carted off the field and taken by ambulance to a nearby hospital after taking a late hit to the head. That makes their bye week well-timed, but it could still be backup Dylan Raiola under center against UCLA. With a Week 2 loss to Oklahoma State already in the books, slipping to 3-2 on the year would be a crushing blow to their already dinged College Football Playoff hopes.

Week 5 Result: LOSS vs. Ohio State (14-31) Next Week: at Washington

After allowing 32 total points through their first four games, the Iowa defense was unable to contain Ohio State's high-powered offense. The Hawkeyes surrendered 324 passing yards, 160 rushing yards and 25 first downs, and Jeremiah Smith torched their secondary for 11 catches, 206 yards and two touchdowns. Iowa's two turnovers were also answered by Ohio State touchdowns, as the Buckeyes fully capitalized on their mistakes.

Week 5 Result: WIN at Virginia Tech (35-33) Next Week: vs. North Carolina

Virginia Tech and Pitt were picked to finish eighth and ninth, respectively, in the ACC's preseason media poll. However, both teams entered Friday's matchup undefeated with a good chance the winner would be part of next week's AP Top 25. The Panthers survived thanks to four Virginia Tech turnovers and a missed field goal as time expired, but they lost quarterback Mason Heintschel to injury early in the second half. He was later seen on crutches , with backup Holden Gernier (8/12, 78 yards, 1 TD) piloting the go-ahead touchdown drive early in the fourth quarter.

21. Oklahoma State (3-1, Previous Rank: 21)

Since starting the year with a head-scratching loss to Tulsa, the Cowboys have victories over then-No. 6 Oregon and previously undefeated West Virginia sandwiched around a blowout of Murray State, putting them back on the national radar. Drew Mestemaker entered Week 5 leading the Big 12 in passing yards (1,271) and passing touchdowns (11). However, he also has five interceptions, and the team has twice as many turnovers (8) as takeaways (4) through four games.

Week 5 Result: WIN vs. Maryland (48-23) Next Week: vs. Indiana

The Cornhuskers are off to their best start since 2016, when they went 7-0 and climbed to No. 7 in the AP poll before finishing 2-4 in their final six games. Anthony Colandrea had 238 passing yards, 108 rushing yards and three touchdowns as he continues to be one of the most impactful transfer quarterbacks in the country. With 20 unanswered points in the fourth quarter, Nebraska turned what was a close game for three quarters into a blowout.

Week 5 Result: WIN vs. Washington (25-21) Next Week: at Penn State

In a relatively quiet game for Jayden Maiava (21/34, 245 yards, 1 TD, 1 INT) and the Trojans offense, the USC defense stepped up when it mattered. They held Washington to 1-for-12 on third-down conversions, forced six punts and halted a 15-play, 77-yard drive on the Huskies' final possession at the USC 18-yard line to preserve the victory.

While they lack a true signature win, the Bruins have played four power conference opponents during their 4-0 start, beating Cal, San Diego State, Purdue and Maryland. They average a staggering 281.5 rushing yards per game, trailing only Army, Air Force, Navy and West Virginia in ground production. If they can survive Oregon coming out of the bye week, their conference schedule does not include Ohio State, Indiana or Iowa.

17. Mississippi State (4-1, Previous Rank: 9)

Week 5 Result: LOSS vs. Alabama (23-56) Next Week: BYE

With two interceptions and a lost fumble, Kamario Taylor finally looked like a true freshman against the Alabama defense. He still had 258 passing yards and three touchdowns, but the giveaways contributed to a close game devolving into a blowout. The Bulldogs were forced to lean on his arm as the rushing game produced just 18 yards on 30 carries, and now they'll have a week to regroup before a road matchup against LSU on Oct. 17.

Week 5 Result: BYE Next Week: at Georgia Tech

The Blue Devils were dealt a blow when Darian Mensah left for Miami in the transfer portal, but that has not stopped them from opening the season 4-0 for the third time in the last four years. Running back Nate Shepard (91 carries, 644 rushing yards, 6 TD) leads the nation in rushing through four weeks, and they have outscored the opposition by a 145-44 margin during their undefeated start. They don't play a ranked opponent until Nov. 4 at Miami, though they do have a quality road win against Illinois on their resume.

Week 5 Result: WIN vs. Auburn (24-14) Next Week: at Arkansas

After recording seven punts and two turnovers on downs last week against Texas, the Tennessee offense struggled to find any momentum once again on Saturday before making a change at quarterback. Backup George MacIntyre completed 8-of-10 passes for 86 yards in relief, and running back DeSean Bishop carried the football 34 times for 220 yards and three second-half touchdowns to turn the tides offensively.

Week 5 Result: LOSS at Missouri (17-45) Next Week: vs. South Carolina

One week after a lopsided 52-28 victory over Ole Miss vaulted Florida into the national picture, they were on the receiving end of a similar blowout. The Gators pounded out 302 rushing yards against Ole Miss, with Jadan Baugh leading the charge with 29 carries for 142 yards and three touchdowns. That production was nowhere to be found on Saturday, as Baugh finished with 13 yards on 12 carries and the team had just 42 rushing yards.

Week 5 Result: WIN at Colorado (29-7) Next Week: BYE

Colorado head coach Deion Sanders turned to Utah transfer Isaac Wilson for his first start of the year over a struggling Julian Lewis, and the Texas Tech defense welcomed him to action by picking him off three times in a game where they logged four total takeaways. The defense picked up the slack for a Red Raiders offense that finished 3-for-12 on third-down conversions while getting outgained 375-315 by Colorado, adding a pick six as part of a 17-point fourth quarter.

Week 5 Result: WIN vs. Florida (45-17) Next Week: vs. Texas A&M

The recipe for success going into Saturday's matchup against Florida was to bottle up their running game and attack their defense with workhorse running back Jamal Roberts. They held the Gators to 42 yards on 25 carries, and Roberts finished with 24 carries for 211 yards and three touchdowns in a game that Missouri dominated from the second quarter on. A road loss to a good Mississippi State team stands as the only blemish on Missouri's resume.

Week 5 Result: BYE Next Week: vs. Kansas

The Utes are 4-0 with a clear path to get to 6-0 with Kansas and Colorado up next after their bye week, but that is followed by a grueling three-week stretch of games against Houston, Cincinnati and BYU. Dual-threat quarterback Devon Dampier has not done much damage with his legs yet this year, but he has taken a significant step forward with his efficiency in the passing game, raising his completion percentage (63.5% to 70.3%) while also improving his yards per attempt (7.5 to 8.9).

Colorado State DC gets fired mid-game during blowout loss

Week 5 Result: BYE Next Week: at Vanderbilt

Despite a lopsided 52-28 loss to Florida in Week 4, this is still a dangerous Ole Miss team with quality wins over Louisville and LSU prior to that shellacking in Gainesville. Only 11 FBS teams are allowing more rushing yards per game than the 194.8 surrendered by the Ole Miss defense, though those numbers are skewed a bit by the staggering 302 yards they allowed last week. Heisman candidate Trinidad Chambliss enters Week 5 leading the SEC in passing yards (1,222) while tallying 12 total touchdowns.'

Week 5 Result: WIN vs. McNeese (63-14) Next Week: at Kentucky

While the rest of the SEC was either battling head-to-head or on a bye week, LSU had a Week 5 cupcake against McNeese that they entered as 53.5-point favorites. The final score was not quite that lopsided, but the outcome was never in doubt, as the Tigers finished with a staggering 731-196 advantage in total yardage. McNeese had more punts (10) than first downs (6), though they did find the end zone on back-to-back possessions in the third quarter.

Week 5 Result: WIN at TCU (17-10) Next Week: vs. Iowa State

Despite just 216 total yards of offense, BYU was able to grind out a conference win on the road against TCU to improve to 4-0 for the third year in a row. Quarterback Bear Bachmeier scored what turned out to be the game-winning touchdown with a 21-yard run to cap off a 10-play, 72-yard drive that spanned nearly six minutes of game time. He threw for just 62 yards, but had 68 rushing yards and two touchdowns on 15 carries to provide the bulk of the offensive production.

Week 5 Result: WIN at Iowa (31-14) Next Week: vs. Maryland

The story going into Saturday's game was Ohio State's offense against Iowa's defense, and the Buckeyes won that battle decisively. Julian Sayin (20/27, 324 yards, 3 TD, 0 INT) and Jeremiah Smith (11 catches, 206 yards, 2 TD) put together another eye-popping performance through the air, while Ja'Kobi Jackson and Bo Jackson combined for 142 rushing yards on 30 carries. It was a quality road win against an Iowa team that had climbed all the way to No. 14 in the latest AP poll.

Week 5 Result: WIN at Rutgers (47-15) Next Week: at Nebraska

The list of offensive standouts was a long one in a game where Indiana hung almost 600 yards of total offense on an overmatched Rutgers defense. Josh Hoover (20/27, 251 yards, 4 TD, 0 INT) had big games with Nick Marsh (7 catches, 120 yards, 1 TD) and Charlie Becker (8 catches, 107 yards, 2 TD) through the air, while Turbo Richard (13 carries, 204 yards, 1 TD) and Lee Bebee Jr. (18 carries, 122 yards, 1 TD) both passed the century mark on the ground. All 15 of Rutgers' points came in the second half, after they fell behind 37-0.

5. Alabama Crimson Tide (5-0, Previous Rank: 8)

Week 5 Result: WIN at Mississippi State (56-23) Next Week: vs. Georgia

The Crimson Tide scored touchdowns on five straight possessions, starting with their final drive of the first half and running through the fourth quarter, turning a 21-14 game into a blowout by the time the final whistle sounded.

Keelon Russell won the battle of breakout quarterbacks against Kamario Taylor, completing 16-of-22 pass attempts for 285 yards and three touchdowns while also scoring his fourth rushing touchdown of the year.

On the defensive end, they controlled the game with four takeaways, five sacks and nine tackles for loss. The impressive victory adds even more juice to next weekend's matchup against Georgia.

4. Miami Hurricanes (5-0, Previous Rank: 4)

Week 5 Result: WIN at Clemson (41-13) Next Week: BYE

Props to the Clemson defense for slowing down Darian Mensah (18/27, 227 yard, 1 TD, 0 INT) and Malachi Toney (5 catches, 40 yards).

However, the Hurricanes running game picked up the slack, with Mark Fletcher Jr. (16 carries, 77 yards, 2 TD) leading a group that finished with 192 yards and three scores. Mensah also added a 34-yard rushing score.

On the flip side, the run defense surrendered just 55 yards on 31 carries, forcing true freshman quarterback Tait Reynolds to attempt a season-high 41 passes. With that, the Hurricanes passed one of the toughest tests on their schedule with flying colors.

3. Notre Dame Fighting Irish (5-0, Previous Rank: 3)

Week 5 Result: WIN at North Carolina (37-26) Next Week: vs. Stanford

A 98-yard kick return touchdown from North Carolina to open the second half cut Notre Dame's lead to 21-20, but they responded with 17 unanswered points to regain control and avoid an upset.

The Fighting Irish offense tallied 475 yards, despite sloppy weather, and CJ Carr completed 21-of-29 pass attempts for 234 yards and four touchdowns. He also added a fifth score on the ground, playing a part in all five of the team's scores.

The running game also played a significant role, despite not finding the end zone, piling up a season-high 241 yards on 45 carries. Jonaz Walton led the way with 120 yards on 23 carries.

2. Texas Longhorns (4-0, Previous Rank: 2)

Week 5 Result: BYE Next Week: at Oklahoma

With a victory over then-No. 1 Ohio State and a road win against Tennessee in Week 4, the Longhorns have already put together an impressive resume, even if they only won those two games by a combined four points.

Arch Manning (63.5 cmp%, 862 yards, 7 TD, 3 INT) is not having the Heisman-caliber season many were expecting, but the running back tandem of Hollywood Smothers and Raleek Brown has been productive, leading a rushing attack averaging 147.3 yards per game.

The real strength of the team has been a defense that ranks inside the top 20 nationally in total yards allowed per game (271.0, 20th) and points allowed per game (13.3, 16th). Edge rusher Colin Simmons is off to a dizzying start with nine tackles for loss, 7.5 sacks and one forced fumble.

1. Georgia Bulldogs (5-0, Previous Rank: 1)

Week 5 Result: WIN vs. Vanderbilt (38-14) Next Week: at Alabama

The Bulldogs led 21-14 at halftime in a game where they were 25.5-point favorites, and they still almost covered that spread by outscoring the Commodores 17-0 after the break.

Quarterback Gunner Stockton had an efficient game under center, completing 25-of-32 passes for 295 yards and three touchdowns, and 10 different players caught a pass as he spread it around nicely in the passing game.

The Commodores had just 49 yards of offense in the second half, including a 10-play, 35-yard drive that spanned seven minutes and ended in a turnover on downs immediately following a Georgia touchdown.

articles.title: Cavan Sullivan Makes History, USMNT vs. Mexico Score, Highlights, Stats and Reaction
articles.summary: The United States Men's National Team took down Mexico in a friendly on Saturday, securing a 3-0 win over its rival at State Farm Stadium.
articles.body:
The United States Men's National Team took down Mexico in a friendly on Saturday, securing a 3-0 win over its rival at State Farm Stadium.

Cavan Sullivan made history for the Americans by finding the back of the net during the win, becoming the youngest goal-scorer in USMNT history at 17 years and five days old.

Colorado State DC gets fired mid-game during blowout loss

Julian Hall and Malik Tillman also picked up goals for the U.S. squad in the victory.

Hall's goal came in the 28th minute, giving the United States a bit of breathing room after withstanding some early pressure from El Tri.

Mexico had an opportunity for a short-range equalizer just before the first half came to a close, but Santiago Giménez was unable to finish with his left foot.

The Mexican team threatened to score again early in the second half, but USMNT goalkeeper Diego Kochen recorded an impressive save.

Sullivan eventually scored to give the Americans a 2-0 lead before a brief altercation between Mateo Chávez and Sebastian Berhalter resulted in a red card for Chávez.

With Mexico down to 10 men, Tillman put the finishing touches on the United States' victory with his goal in the 84th minute.

Although the USMNT only held 49 percent of possession throughout the match, manager Mauricio Pochettino's team finished with four shots on goal compared to just one for Mexico.

The United States has now won three consecutive friendlies since exiting the FIFA World Cup in the round of 16.

articles.title: Chelsea news: Cesar Azpilicueta -  clawed my way to the top but need a break
articles.summary: Cesar Azpilicueta says it is time to move to "a different stage of life" following a glorious 20-year playing career, notably captaining Chelsea to several titles.
articles.body:
Cesar Azpilicueta was an all-encompassing leader for Chelsea - and, now retired, he reflects on how his passion for education and attention to detail helped him build a career at the highest level.

One story sums it up. Before Chelsea 's Champions League final victory in 2021, Azpilicueta could not take his customary pre-match nap and opted to study instead.

He says his work towards an MBA in business management from the Berlin School of Business and Innovation took his mind off the pressure and noise on the streets of Porto.

Later that day, he lifted the Champions League trophy after captaining Chelsea to victory against Manchester City .

Azpilicueta told BBC Sport: "When I was a kid my parents pushed me to get good grades and finish school.

"I wasn't a professional footballer until I was 17, in my last year of school. Education was always important. When Covid-19 arrived, we had more time.

"I found some courses but I didn't start because I thought it was the end of my career. It was more that I wanted to learn, improve myself and do it in another language.

"It wasn't because I thought it was my last year as a footballer, but it did help me navigate the final years of my career, become a better person and a better footballer."

Azpilicueta, 37, was speaking at Arsenal 's Emirates Stadium, where he joked he did not feel "entirely comfortable", while collecting a diploma in global football sport directorship through the PFA Business School, adding to qualifications that also include a diploma from Harvard Business School.

Now retired from playing after spending last season at Sevilla, he replied "maybe" when asked whether he could become a sporting director one day, but says football has left him in need of a post-career break.

Now at a "different stage of life", he cannot even contemplate playing football with friends for fun because it would trigger his competitive instincts.

"It was time to stop playing football because, even though I could probably still play, I didn't have the energy to commit myself fully for an entire season," he reflected.

"At the moment I have another commitment, which is my family. I want to play some golf and enjoy life.

"For 20 years I was constantly travelling, playing and preparing for seasons. This summer looked completely different."

After beginning at boyhood club Osasuna, Azpilicueta joined Marseille, where he learned French. However, it was his move to Chelsea in 2012 that proved transformative.

Completing his latest course highlights Azpilicueta's thirst for knowledge and a desire for constant self-improvement.

It was something he learned at Chelsea , where he arrived as a relatively low-profile £7m signing in a dressing room full of established leaders such as John Terry, Frank Lampard and Petr Cech, alongside star names including Fernando Torres, Eden Hazard and Ashley Cole.

He explained: "I started as a right winger, moved to France, then moved to Chelsea . I wasn't a star signing. I had to find my way. Left-back, wing-back, centre-back in a back three.

"It was about consistency. I had to work hard to stay fit, adapt to different managers and different positions.

"When you arrive at Chelsea , you feel the ambition straight away. Every three days you have to win. Every game and every trophy matters.

"That culture pushed me to the maximum and, especially when I left Chelsea , I felt that I had given everything I had for the club."

Azpilicueta explained how his education away from the pitch helped him develop into a leader at Stamford Bridge.

It gave him the confidence to represent Premier League players during the Covid-19 pandemic, while also helping to organise initiatives and keep the club moving forward after owner Roman Abramovich was sanctioned following Russia's invasion of Ukraine.

His defining moment came in that 2021 Champions League final victory.

There is little doubt that, having succeeded Terry and then Gary Cahill as captain, Azpilicueta ranks among Chelsea 's greatest leaders. Yet he revealed that, since leaving the club in 2023, he has not returned to Stamford Bridge.

He was among dozens of players to leave after Chelsea changed ownership from Abramovich to the current American-led consortium in 2022.

"I left Chelsea , but Chelsea will always stay in my heart," he said. "I follow every game and I hope the club comes back to where it belongs.

"There are some very strong teams around and football sometimes needs a bit of time. You need connections, people playing together and understanding each other.

"At a big club like Chelsea , the demands are high. But I think that's normal. It should be demanding and ambitious because, speaking as a Chelsea fan, you always want to see the club winning trophies.

"I have confidence that [manager] Xabi [Alonso], the staff and the players will do good work. Hopefully they can bring a lot of happiness to the fans."

He has been following Chelsea 's latest captain Reece James, who he believes will grow into a better leader, since over-30 players Jordan Henderson, Danny Welbeck and Emiliano Martinez joined over the summer.

When it is suggested that he might return to Stamford Bridge in some capacity to be marked by a warm reception from supporters, Azpilicueta responds modestly: "I don't know about that.

"I will come back one day. I won't be putting on my boots, though."

articles.title: Yamal scores stunning goal in Spain’s 3-1 Nations League win over Czechia
articles.summary: Lamine Yamal is the first player to score within the first 10 minutes of each of three consecutive men’s football games.
articles.body:
Lamine Yamal has carried on his superb goal-scoring form, helping Spain secure a 3-1 win over Czechia in the UEFA Nations League and consolidating his bid to win the prestigious Ballon d’Or award later this month.

The world champions moved three points clear of England at the top of Group A3 after Thomas Tuchel’s side demolished Croatia 7-0 earlier in Rijeka on Saturday.

Spain cruised into a two-goal lead with Yamal and captain Rodri Hernandez on target, but Jiri Slama gave the Czechs a chance by pulling one back with 20 minutes to go.

However, Mikel Merino wrapped up Spain’s win late on after Ladislav Krejci was sent off for the Czechs, as Spain racked up a 41st consecutive unbeaten game, including the World Cup final win over Argentina in July.

Yamal, who scored in the second minute of Spain’s first two games against England and Croatia, waited as long as the sixth minute before breaking the deadlock. He is the first player to score a goal within the first 10 minutes of three consecutive men’s international matches.

“They are well-drilled; I thought it would be one of the hardest games, and that’s how it was,” Rodri told a Spanish broadcaster after Spain claimed a third win from three group games.

“It was tricky but we got some chances. There are some matches in which you can’t generate that much, but the team was able to manage the match.”

The former Manchester City midfielder scored for the first time for Spain in more than two years.

“It’s always special to score for the national team. I’d not been scoring many goals; let’s see if I’ve found that dynamic – it’s important, we all have to chip in with the goals,” he added.

Spain coach Luis de la Fuente made several changes in Oviedo from Tuesday’s win over Croatia, including handing debuts to full-back Ivan Fresneda and striker Roberto Fernandez.

It was one of Spain’s star names, though, who lit up the game early on, something he is beginning to make a habit of.

The 19-year-old winger, a leading candidate for the Ballon d’Or, produced an exquisite finish from the right of the box, curling into the top corner after taking a touch to earn himself room to shoot.

“We’re doing well; I’m very happy. I was eager to return to the national team after the World Cup, and there’s no better way than this,” said Yamal.

Spain coach De la Fuente put his hands to his head in apparent shock at the quality of Yamal’s superb strike, his 12th in his last nine games for club and country.

“I think he never stops surprising us – I think all of us. He has so much talent, so much quality, that we still haven’t seen the best version of Lamine by a long shot,” said De la Fuente.

“He has a lot more to offer because he’s so classy, so talented, with so much potential.”

The winger’s Barcelona teammate, Rodri, doubled Spain’s lead after 35 minutes, arriving in the box to drill into the top corner after the ball fell nicely for him.

De la Fuente took off Yamal at half-time to give the young Barcelona star a break before Tuesday’s visit to face Croatia, and the pace of the game slowed.

The Czechs pulled one back through Slama, who produced an excellent low finish across David Raya after Adam Hlozek played him in.

Arsenal stopper Raya was fortunate a few minutes later when he conceded possession with a misplaced pass while out of his goal, but the visitors could not capitalise.

Raya also spilled the ball badly and Ryan Naderi turned home, but the goal was disallowed for a foul on Robin Le Normand.

Czechia’s determined efforts to battle back were derailed by Krejci’s red card, with the defender shown a second yellow for pulling back Fernandez, before Merino rounded off Spain’s win.

articles.title: World Grand Prix Darts: Luke Humphries says reaching final 'doesn't mean anything' without beating Gerwyn Price to title
articles.summary: Luke Humphries and Gerwyn Price will meet in Sunday’s World Grand Prix final; Humphries beat Price to the 2023 title but has been runner-up in the last two years at the Mattioli Arena; watch live from 8pm on Sky Sports Main Event
articles.body:
Humphries made history by becoming the first player to reach the final in four consecutive years at the double-in event, defeating James Wade 5-3 to book his place in Sunday's showpiece at the Mattioli Arena.

'Cool Hand' was runner-up to Luke Littler after a 6-1 thrashing last year and suffered a shock 6-4 loss to Mike de Decker in 2024, with Humphries now hoping for a repeat of his 2023 victory over Price when the two former world champions meet again at the final.

"It has been one of those journeys this year that hasn't been playing sailing," Humphries told Sky Sports . "A few of the years before have felt a lot easier than it has done this year.

"To make four Grand Prix finals on the trot is super special. It's history for myself and I'm proud of that but, unless I pick that trophy up, unfortunately that history doesn't mean anything.

"I've come here to win it. If I win the trophy, I'll look back at the history and think that's amazing."

Humphries has had a string of runner-up finishes in TV finals since winning the Premier League in May 2025, including the European Championship and Grand Slam of Darts in 2025 and this year's Premier League final, but is determined to end that record.

"The way I haven't been playing hasn't been the best, but the way I've bounced back and performed in that way is great," Humphries added. "I've got to do it again tomorrow because there's so many major finals I've let slip.

"I don't think I was far from my best. The scoring was pretty decent and the doubling in was good. I felt like that was the most controlled consisted performance I've put in for a long time.

"The last time I felt like that was maybe the Premier League final against Luke [Littler]. It's been a long time since I've felt that control and not like I was going to flounder a little bit.

"Gezzy [Price] is playing well but if I play like that again, it's going to be a cracking game and I hope it is. I'm going to come back tomorrow [Sunday] fresh and believe I can do that again and play even better."

2020 champion Price is through to his fourth World Grand Prix final and first since losing to Humphries in 2023, with the Welshman frustrated by Nathan Aspinall during his 5-2 victory in the opening semi-final.

"Nathan [Aspinall] was complaining about the crowd but they were on his side," Price told Sky Sports . "I'm 3-0 up and I go back and say to Nathan 'they're on your side bud, come on. Stop performing on the board and just play darts'.

"I was a little bit upset with him. As good as the crowd is for me, they were all for him. He's performing a little bit on stage and I told him I wasn't happy. I'm great friends with Nathan but sometimes you've just got to let your darts go - when you're losing you're losing."

Price added: "I was frustrated 90 per cent of that game and it's not good. I think it was a bit of a poor game, it was up and down. In patches, I'm playing well. When my game is there, I'm playing some of the best stuff in the world.

"I'm here to win trophies and money, but I'm into another final, third one on the bounce - happy days!"

Mardle expects 'brilliant final' between two past champions

"He [Humphries] feels that that was somewhere near his best and that's confidence. I don't think Gezzy [Price] was at all impressive tonight. I know he won, I just feel that Luke going into that final now will obviously fancy it.

"I think it's really impressive the way that he [Humphries] has actually had to play better and did play better in the two games he's had to do it - putting those bad performances behind him and not worrying about them is growth.

"It's easy to look back and think that Luke's been inconsistent, but so has Gezzy, to a point. Who was the star of the opening round? It was Price. He played fantasticly but, since then, he hasn't reached those heights - it doesn't mean that he can't again.

"What we both want, what we all want, is for the pair of them to come out guns blazing. Then, then we could have a brilliant final on our hands - I just hope it works out that way."

articles.title: Hakan - The Spark
articles.summary: The 2022/23 season seemed to be over before it had even begun. For the first time, there was going to be a break for the World Cup in the middle of the campa...
articles.body:
The 2022/23 season seemed to be over before it had even begun. For the first time, there was going to be a break for the World Cup in the middle of the campaign, while the season itself had started as early as the weekend before Ferragosto. It was not a great start for Inter: four defeats in the first eight matches, eight points behind league leaders Napoli and the Scudetto already looking like a distant dream. Things were no better in Europe: Inter lost their opening home game against Bayern, who looked to be a team in a completely different class. After winning their second match in Plzen, there were two games against Barcelona to come. Another opponent who, on paper, seemed impossible to overcome.

Another problem for Simone Inzaghi: Brozović was ruled out with a muscular problem and Asllani, his natural replacement, had not looked particularly comfortable in the role in the 2-1 defeat to Roma a few days earlier, partly because he had had little time to settle into the position. The newspapers on that 4 October four years ago reported a battle for the regista role between Mkhitaryan and Çalhanoğlu. With the benefit of hindsight, it was the match that changed the Turk's career and Inter's European history. Against a phenomenal team, particularly from midfield upwards; Gavi, Pedri, Busquets, Raphinha, Lewandowski, Dembélé. Çalhanoğlu produced an incredible performance: long balls, tackles, constantly making himself available for the ball and finding ways through Barcelona's relentless press. As if that were not enough, he scored the only goal of the match, a low drive from outside the box in the final action of the first half.

There was a bit of everything: a goal ruled out by the narrowest of margins, Joaquín Correa set off from inside his own half, rounded Ter Stegen and slotted into an empty net: a moment of brilliance, unfortunately ruled out. Another Barcelona goal was disallowed for a handball by Ansu Fati, a penalty claimed by the Blaugrana , and the usual roar of San Siro, which on nights like these forgets all about the present, the league table and the problems, transforming into a cauldron of noise. From then on, Inter held on to those three points and their advantage over the Catalans, using them first to secure qualification for the last 16 and then to embark on a memorable European campaign that would only come to an end just metres from the finish line on a night in Istanbul.

From that point onwards, Çalhanoğlu and Inzaghi realised that the Turk could offer his best in that position, while Barcelona developed a strange Nerazzurri syndrome that prevented them from beating Inter, even when they were the stronger side on paper. And there was a recurrence, too. Barcelona and Inter would meet three more times in the Champions League, and from that day onwards the overall score reads 10-9 in Inter's favour. Nineteen goals. Not a single one is worth forgetting.

On 19 May, Steve Clarke assembled his collection of players to embark on a World Cup journey.

Despite featuring and scoring for a Hellas Verona side heading for relegation from Serie A, and with a perennial problem of strikers not firing regularly for Scotland, Kieron Bowie was overlooked.

Given the loyalty Clarke showed to those who had served him so well, it was not a huge surprise. Neither was the impotence of the national team in the USA as they conjured up just one John McGinn goal.

"I received a message from him saying that I'm not in the squad but these things happen and it's just about how you bounce back from it to be honest," said Bowie.

"I scored goals in a struggling Verona team and that was as much as I could do. I was happy with where I was at and I was happy with how I'd played.

"I just spent a lot of time at home with my family and then a little golf holiday to Portugal for a week and that was all I did."

Two going on four, five or six on good night for new Scotland era

Scotland beat North Macedonia in Nations League for Pocognoli's first win

Bowie may have been cursing his luck again on Tuesday when his first international start was reduced to a mere 13 minutes following Jack Hendry's red card in the Hampden loss to Switzerland.

The former Raith Rovers and Hibernian forward was one of the main Scotland heroes in Skopje after sending a deliciously whipped finish into the net in the 2-0 win over North Macedonia.

Playing in a new 3-4-1-2, Bowie started the game up top with Oli McBurnie in an ultra-attacking line up set out by Sebastien Pocognoli.

Throughout the game, his stats stacked up. The most shots with seven, the most on target with four, most shots in the box with five and the most touches in the opposition box with 11.

"You play all your life to represent a country and to score a goal is just an unbelievable feeling," said the 24-year-old Fifer.

"This manager's come in and he's put a lot of trust in me.

"I think the style that he wants to play definitely plays into my strengths. I think you've seen today a lot of times running them in behind and just showing strength against occupying defenders is one of the main things.

"It's a process but I think everyone's enjoying that process and it's a bit of a change."

The word "process" has been used so many times by the Scotland head coach and his players in recent days it's probably the new team motto.

Pocognoli is trying to implement a radically different system to his predecessor. Not only that, it's a different mindset. All while trying to embed a clutch of new players.

It's early days for the Belgian, his group, and, of course, Bowie. But the man on loan at Sassuolo believes things are clicking, and it's an opportunity for him to make his mark.

"It's a lot longer international break," he explained. "We spend a lot more time together so it's good for him to get his message across and his ideas. Also, we play more games so we have to train a little bit less of course.

"I think for me it's a fresh start with a new coach and different ideas.

"He said to me 'you don't need to prove yourself, just go and do what I know you can do' and I feel like I'm just doing that."

Bowie, who made his Rovers debut at 16, added: "I think people, obviously Scottish fans, have the same idea of how I was when I was at Hibs and that's all they can remember.

"But I feel like since I moved to Serie A, it's a different league, different challenge and I'm getting more experience at a higher level.

"So, yeah, I feel like I've definitely kicked into another gear and I feel like I'm showing that."
